review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered result is a matched logarithmic minimax characterization only for the fixed-dimensional, known-envelope Fourier class, with the causal lower bound established on an explicit three-variable exponent-two subclass; the broader Sanjaroonpouri–Ramazi class receives lower-bound transfer only. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor restriction and known ray exponents substantially limit direct applicability, and the package supplies no implemented or empirical demonstration that the proposed regions are informative in the cited IDA/yeast workflow. The manuscript also retains oeq:smooth-splice, calling the construction genuinely open, even though thm:smooth-splice-pair subsequently purports to prove exactly that construction; this stale status contradiction must be removed and the theorem proof treated as the operative claim. These scope and evidence limitations keep the projected leading-journal score below the strongest matched-minimax benchmark, but they do not negate the proved same-class upper and lower rates, collision-stable whole-fiber inference, or the root-N Laplace boundary. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves matched logarithmic covariance and whole-fiber Hausdorff rates only on the fixed three-variable exponent-two subclass; over the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class it proves lower bounds alone, as the framing correctly acknowledges. The causal interpretation remains confined to laws satisfying the explicit greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition and known raywise Fourier envelopes and exponents, so this is not general mixed-noise inference. The motivating pcalg and yeast workflow is not implemented or empirically demonstrated, which limits the significance case for a leading econometrics journal. The Parseval identity is used as a leaf lemma without proof or a precise citation; although classical, the note should cite an exact Plancherel/Parseval result covering the stated convention. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
